key_insight: Reintroduces and advocates for 'Reusability Reports' and stronger code-reporting practices to restore reproducibility and reuse in a rapidly accelerating, LLM-driven research landscape. Clear, standardized reporting lowers the barrier for verification and practical reuse of models and code.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between rapid publication ('fast science') and the ability to reproduce or reuse reported AI/ML work due to inconsistent code sharing, missing environment details, unclear licensing, and limited reporting standards.
method: Promote an article format ('Reusability Reports') that highlights exemplary code-sharing and reporting practices alongside research results.
Recommend concrete reporting elements (code availability, data access, environment/config, licensing, usage examples) and simple checklists to increase transparency and reuse.
Advocate community incentives and editorial policies to recognize and reward reproducible, reusable artifacts in AI publications.
impact: Improved reporting and standardized reusability practices make AI research easier to verify, extend, and deploy—accelerating trustworthy progress while reducing wasted effort and fragile, non-reproducible work.
visual_elements: Flowchart of a Reusability Report showing sections: Code → Data → Environment → License → Usage Example
Before/After comparison: fast-science paper with missing artifacts vs. paper with full Reusability Report
Checklist infographic (icons) for the five essential reproducibility items: code, data, env, license, demo
Bar or timeline chart illustrating reduced time-to-reuse and higher verification rates when Reusability Reports are adopted
paper_title: Recognizing reproducibility and reusability in times of fast science
